name: Curtain wall
summary: A thin outer wall of glass and metal that hangs on the frame of the building and carries no floor load.
how: Carry the floors on columns set 1 to 3 m back from the facade line.
Hang the glass in a grid of mullions at 1.2 to 1.5 m centres.
Keep the glass part of the facade above 60%.

origin.note: The Hallidie Building of Willis Polk hangs a glass wall in front of a concrete frame.

adoptions.via: The workshop wing of the Bauhaus Dessau hangs a three-storey glass wall in front of its frame.
Lever House in New York wraps a slab of offices in green glass and steel.
Norman Foster hangs a frameless glass wall from the roof of the Willis Faber and Dumas building in Ipswich.

sources.title: Kenneth Frampton, Modern Architecture: A Critical History (1980)
